findings.claim: The index marker is appended to the line that holds the link, so on a wrapped index entry it lands in the middle of the description. This repository's own decisions index wraps every entry, so the first real use corrupts it.
test_supersede_links_both_ways checks only for "## Correction, " and never checks that a date follows, so an undated section passes r2's fails_when.

test_supersede_refusals checks only for a nonzero exit, so an uncaught exception (exit 1 with a traceback) passes as a refusal. It should assert the one-line "refused:" message on stderr, and it does not cover the same-id or missing-index-entry refusals.
_number uses str.isdigit, which accepts Unicode digits such as "²"; int() then raises ValueError and the CLI prints a traceback instead of a refusal.

The cli-interface rule is not fully met. The decision group's help does not name its prerequisites (a bundle from kmctl init, records from kmctl new decision). The already-deprecated and self-supersede refusals name no next command. The missing-index-entry refusal points to kmctl check, which reports the problem but does not fix it.
